```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
# Use an empty registry so the output does not depend on this machine.
old <- options(gambitR3D.registry_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "vignette-registry"))
```

The rules engine and the alpha-beta search need no model. A model is an
optional opponent and analysis aid. This guide covers which models exist, what
each can do, and how to set up the optional training environment.

## What is available

```{r}
caps <- gambitR3D::g3_model_capabilities()
unique(caps[, c("model_id", "kind", "model_status")])
```

- `builtin-search` is the alpha-beta search: always available.
- `builtin-square-transformer` is the package's own architecture: 64
  physical-square tokens, seven board tokens and one global token, with a
  scorer over the legal actions supplied by the rules engine and a
  win/draw/loss head. Until you train it, it is an untrained architecture and
  cannot play.
- Three published ordinary-chess models are listed for reference only. They
  were trained on 8×8 chess with fixed move vocabularies; none of them can
  represent platforms, overlapping squares or this game's actions. They are
  marked "adaptation required", are never downloaded automatically and cannot
  play. A declared licence on a model card is recorded as a declaration, not as
  proof of rights.

```{r}
caps[caps$model_id == "builtin-square-transformer", c("task", "status", "reason")]
```

## Compatibility checks

A model is used only after validation: matching rules hash, feature and action
schemas, artifact hashes recomputed in R, complete provenance, the requested
task, and a working runtime. A model that fails any check is refused with the
reason.

```{r}
v <- gambitR3D::g3_validate_model("builtin-square-transformer", error = FALSE)
v$valid
v$checks[v$checks$status != "pass", c("check", "status", "detail")]
```

## The optional training environment

Training and model play use a separate Python environment with a CPU build of
PyTorch, created at a path you choose. It is never touched when the package is
loaded, and installing the package downloads nothing.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Creates the environment with uv from the package's pinned lock (with
# hashes): Python 3.12, CPU-only torch, numpy, safetensors. About 820 MB installed.
env <- file.path(tools::R_user_dir("gambitR3D", "data"), "ml-env")
report <- gambitR3D::g3_setup_ml(env)
report
```

The report gives the Python and package versions, the device, and whether the
worker's feature schema matches the R encoder's. It reports `blocked`, with the
reason, when `uv` is missing or no lock exists for the platform; it never
installs unpinned packages. The lock is currently resolved for Linux x86_64.

The worker is a separate process that exchanges JSON lines with R. It computes
tensors only: it never sees the rules and never returns a position. R checks
every reply (request ids, hashes, sizes, finiteness, the digest of the
candidate actions) and maps the scores back to legal action ids.

## Using a trained model

After `vignette("training")`, a validated checkpoint plays like any other
agent:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
st <- gambitR3D::g3_new_game()$state
d <- gambitR3D::g3_choose_action(st, agent = "model:<model id>",
                                 budget = list(mode = "mcts", simulations = 32L))
d$label
pred <- gambitR3D::g3_predict_actions("model:<model id>", st)
head(pred$actions[order(pred$actions$rank), c("label", "probability")])
pred$wdl
```

Model values are from the side to act: win, draw, loss probabilities, value
`p(win) - p(loss)` and expected score `p(win) + 0.5 p(draw)`. They are model
estimates, uncalibrated unless a calibration study says otherwise. A short
training run tests the pipeline; it does not make a strong opponent.

```{r, include = FALSE}
options(old)
```
